I flagged the headlamp because **the submitted evidence does not connect its replacement to this collision**—not because the part is expensive or because damage has been ruled out.

| Source | What it establishes |
|---|---|
| **Repair estimate DOC-10482-08, page 1, line 1** | Requests **“Repl — Headlamp assy LT, LED”** for **$1,240.00**: a **$1,165.00** part plus **0.6 mechanical labor hours**. “LT” means the **left-front headlamp**, away from the estimate’s stated **“05 Right Rear”** impact. No explanation connects that replacement to the impact. |
| **Claim record and claim form DOC-10482-01, page 1** | Describe damage to the **rear bumper, right-rear quarter panel and right tail lamp**. They do not report left-headlamp damage. |
| **Police report DOC-10482-07, pages 1–2** | Records right-rear impact, a cracked/pushed-in rear bumper cover, creased/scraped right-rear quarter panel and broken right tail-lamp lens. It does not describe left-headlamp damage or a secondary impact affecting it. |
| **Photographs DOC-10482-02–06** | My observations of the rear/right views support the documented right-rear damage. **DOC-10482-06, “Front and left side of vehicle,”** includes the left headlamp, but distance, angle and reflections limit assessment. It does **not establish damage requiring replacement**; it also does not prove the lamp is undamaged. |

**Contoso’s rule:** Repair Estimate Review Guidelines §§10.1–10.2 calls for supporting information when a line repairs an area away from the reported impact without an explanation connecting it to the loss. The affected line stays in manual review while supported lines continue.  Auto Claims Handling Guidelines §§8–9 also says an overall photograph or an officer’s limited damage observations cannot rule out damage elsewhere. 

**What would resolve it:** Ask Harborline for clear left-headlamp close-ups, inspection findings and an explanation of how this collision caused the damage—or a corrected estimate if the line was entered in error. This remains an ordinary evidence clarification, not an allegation of wrongdoing.
